newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin mulls cabinet reorganisation, some changes.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin mulls cabinet reorganisation, some changes.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin, alarmed by rising social strife, said on Monday some ministers might have to go or the government structure changed to solve the problem.

"Maybe we need some changes, maybe we need some names, maybe we need some people to be changed in the government," he told Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin during a meeting in Kremlin. His remarks were broadcast on television.

"An opinion poll showed that most Russians were unhappy with the government, the premier and the president... The main thing is that the government cannot cope with (delayed) pensions, wages and payments," said Yeltsin, looking determined and speaking very clearly.
"I am the president and I am responsible for the work of the government. Tell me who needs to be replaced and I will listen to your opinion," he told Chernomyrdin.
He said the main thing was to make government more efficient without racing into ill-considered decisions.
Yeltsin made his first public appearance on Sunday after almost two months in hospital and at his country residence recovering from pneumonia. He looked thin but lively.
Chernomyrdin told Yeltsin he agreed with him, but said regional authorities were partly to blame for social problems.
